summary: Milestone 2026.09.664 completed 9 experiments, all compute-bound, in 5.7 wall-time minutes. The longest task was 'Qualify bounded Qwen evidence pointers and capture feasibility' at 1.47 minutes, followed by 'Qualify matched-history replay from the live agents own attempts' at 1.34 minutes and 'Bind fourteen tasks and ingest qualified evidence methods' at 0.87 minutes. Sub-phase timing was not recorded within these runs to separate model inference duration from validation scaffolding or artifact serialization overhead.
bottlenecks_identified: 'Qualify bounded Qwen evidence pointers and capture feasibility' was the longest task at 1.47 minutes out of 5.7 total wall-time minutes (approx. 26% of milestone duration), but lacks granular sub-phase instrumentation to isolate model inference latency from validation scaffolding and disk serialization.

'Qualify matched-history replay from the live agents own attempts' (1.34 minutes) and 'Bind fourteen tasks and ingest qualified evidence methods' (0.87 minutes) combined with the longest task to account for 3.68 minutes (approx. 65% of total milestone wall time) without recorded intra-task phase durations.

The top 5 experiments accounted for 4.90 out of 5.7 total wall-time minutes (approx. 86% of execution time), with milestone timings reconstructed from disk mtimes rather than continuous runtime execution logging.

The GPU monitor report provides an isolated post-completion snapshot (PID 772157 on GPU 0 with 18054MB allocated at 0% utilization, GPU 1 idle at 4MB), leaving GPU utilization across active compute execution windows unmeasured (with gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks locked to false).
Task launch records did not log model concurrency or runner dispatch details, although all completed tasks were single-model runs where DualGPURunner multi-model dispatch is not applicable.
improvements_suggested: Instrument granular sub-phase duration timers and monotonic stage logging inside compute-bound workflows to isolate model inference latency from verification scaffolding and disk serialization.

Deploy continuous, task-aligned accelerator telemetry during compute-bound executions to sample live GPU utilization and VRAM occupancy across active compute windows rather than relying on point-in-time post-run snapshots.
Record explicit model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment task receipts to audit DualGPURunner eligibility whenever two or more models run concurrently.
Implement runtime milestone-scoped execution logging to avoid reliance on post-hoc disk-mtime timing reconstruction.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument sub-phase duration timers and per-stage progress logging inside the Qwen evidence capture and matched-history replay pipelines.
Deploy continuous accelerator telemetry during compute-bound task execution to record live GPU utilization and VRAM occupancy across active execution windows.
Emit explicit model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment receipts to audit DualGPURunner engagement on multi-model workloads.
meta_reflection: The milestone completed 9 compute-bound tasks in 5.7 wall-time minutes, with execution concentrated in Qwen evidence capture (1.47 minutes), matched-history replay qualification (1.34 minutes), and task binding / evidence ingestion (0.87 minutes). The post-run GPU monitor report confirms an idle llama.cpp process on GPU 0 after completion but cannot evaluate active-window compute efficiency, and because only single-model tasks were executed, no DualGPURunner multi-model dispatch opportunity was missed. Sub-phase timing and continuous execution telemetry are necessary next steps to identify actionable latency optimizations.
